sections.title: Project Overview & Goals
sections.description: MockMate is a full-stack, AI-powered interview simulation platform. Users configure a mock interview session based on their target job role and experience level, then speak their answers aloud while the AI dynamically generates follow-up questions, evaluates responses, and delivers structured feedback.
sections.core_mission: Give developers a realistic, repeatable interview practice experience powered by a context-aware LLM — accessible from any browser, free at its core, and deployable in 14 days.
key_features: Real-time voice input (Speech-to-Text) and AI voice output (Text-to-Speech)
Webcam integration for psychological 'real interview' feel
Post-interview analytics: radar chart, per-question breakdown, overall score
Secure auth, route protection, and user-scoped data
guiding_principles: Core Logic First: The AI conversation engine is built and tested before any UI polish
No Resume Fluff: Every tech choice serves a function, not just a buzzword
Speed: Use managed services (Firebase, Clerk, Vercel) to eliminate DevOps overhead
Security: Users never access another user's interview data

data_flow.title: High-Level Data Flow (One Full Interview Turn)
steps: User speaks answer → Browser Web Speech API captures audio → transcribes to text string.
Frontend stores text in React state (userAnswer). User clicks 'Submit Answer'.
Frontend calls POST /api/generate-question with { interviewId, userAnswer }.
API Route: Queries Firebase for last N messages in this session.
API Route: Constructs full prompt = System Prompt + Chat History + New User Answer.
API Route: Sends prompt to Gemini 1.5 Flash via Google Generative AI SDK.
Gemini returns next question as text. API saves Question+Answer pair to Firebase.
API returns { question } to frontend. Frontend uses window.speechSynthesis to speak it aloud.
Process repeats until question count reaches limit (e.g., 5 questions).

statelessness_problem.title: Statelessness & the Memory Problem
statelessness_problem.critical_concept: Gemini (and all LLMs) are stateless. Each API call is independent — the model has zero memory of previous calls. To simulate a continuous conversation, you must manually attach the entire conversation history to every single API request. This is the core engineering challenge of the project.

sections.title: The AI Brain — Core Logic Deep Dive
sections.description: This is the most important section. Build this correctly and everything else is just UI wiring.

system_prompt.title: The System Prompt (Interviewer Personality)
system_prompt.description: The System Prompt is sent ONCE at the beginning of the Gemini chat session. It defines who the AI is, how it behaves, and what rules it must follow.
system_prompt.template:
You are an expert senior technical interviewer conducting a mock interview.
The candidate is applying for: {jobRole}
Years of experience claimed: {experience}
Job Description context: {jobDesc}

YOUR RULES:
1. Ask exactly ONE question per turn.
2. Start with a warm-up, then increase difficulty.
3. If the answer is vague, ask ONE targeted follow-up.
4. Do NOT reveal answers. Probe deeper instead.
5. Cover: Core Concepts, System Design, Problem Solving, Past Experience, Cultural Fit.
6. Keep questions relevant to the job description.
7. Be professional, concise, and encouraging.
8. After 5 exchanges, respond ONLY with: [INTERVIEW_COMPLETE]

context_builder.title: The Context Builder
context_builder.description: Before every Gemini API call, reconstruct the full conversation from the database and format it into the structure Gemini expects.

api_route_generate_question.title: API Route: /api/generate-question
steps: Verify Clerk auth — return 401 if unauthenticated
Fetch MockInterview record with all messages ordered by createdAt ASC
Build system prompt using buildSystemPrompt()
Format chatHistory as Gemini Message[] (model/user role pairs)
Call generateNextQuestion() with full context
Check if response contains [INTERVIEW_COMPLETE]
Persist Q&A pair to UserAnswer table
Return { question, isComplete }

feedback_engine.title: The Feedback Engine
feedback_engine.description: After interview ends, send full transcript to Gemini with evaluation prompt. Requests structured JSON feedback.

sections.title: Voice Integration (STT + TTS)
sections.description: Voice makes MockMate feel like a real interview. Use browser-native APIs — no third-party voice service needed.

subsections.critical_ux_pattern: The flow must be: AI speaks question → onEnd callback fires → mic activates automatically. NEVER activate mic while AI is speaking — you will capture the AI's own voice as user input.

sections.title: 14-Day Execution Roadmap
sections.note: Each day assumes 2-3 hours of focused work. Core logic is prioritized in Phase 2. Do not skip or reorder phases.

tasks.task: npx create-next-app@latest. Install Clerk, configure .env.local. Confirm /dashboard redirects to login.
Create Firebase project. Install Prisma. Write schema.prisma. Run: prisma db push. Seed one test record.
Build shared Navbar and Footer. Build landing page Hero section. Deploy to Vercel early.
Build Dashboard UI with static mock data. Build 'New Interview' form dialog (UI only, no submit logic yet).
Get Gemini API key. Install @google/generative-ai. Write lib/gemini.ts and lib/prompts.ts. Test with Node.js script.
Connect 'New Interview' form to database. POST /api/interview/create saves record. Redirect to /interview/[id].
Install react-webcam and react-speech-recognition. Build Interview Room layout. Hook up mic — print transcript to screen.
Build POST /api/generate-question (full implementation). Wire frontend: speak → API → question → TTS. THIS IS THE CORE FEATURE.
Save every Q&A pair to DB. Add question counter. Build 'End Interview' flow redirecting to feedback page.
Build POST /api/generate-feedback. Send full transcript to Gemini with evaluation prompt. Parse JSON response.
Install recharts. Build Feedback Page: RadialBarChart for score, RadarChart for dimensions, Accordion for Q&A.
Build Settings page with Clerk <UserProfile />. Add middleware. Test that User A cannot access User B's interview data.
Bug fixes. Add Shadcn Skeleton loading states everywhere. Test full flow end-to-end. Check mobile responsiveness.
Final Vercel deployment. Add all env vars to Vercel dashboard. Update GitHub README with Live Demo link. DONE.

sections.title: Security Checklist
sections.critical_rule: A user must NEVER be able to view, modify, or delete another user's interview data.

checks.name: Data Isolation
checks.description: Every MockInterview record stores the Clerk userId. On every API route, verify the userId from auth() matches the interview's userId before returning data.

checks.name: API Key Security
checks.description: GEMINI_API_KEY is server-side only — never in NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables.

checks.name: Input Sanitization
checks.description: Trim and limit job description input to prevent prompt injection attacks.

checks.name: Rate Limiting
checks.description: Add per-userId counter for Gemini API calls. Max 5 interviews/day on free tier.

checks.name: HTTPS
checks.description: Vercel provides this automatically — never deploy to HTTP.

sections.title: Deployment Guide (Vercel)
steps: Push code to a GitHub repository.
Go to vercel.com → Import Project → Select your GitHub repo.
In Vercel dashboard: Settings → Environment Variables → add all .env.local variables.
Trigger a new deployment. Vercel auto-detects Next.js and handles build.
Copy live URL → add to GitHub README as 'Live Demo'.
post_deployment_checklist: Test full interview flow end-to-end on the live URL
Verify Clerk OAuth redirect URLs include your Vercel domain
Check Firebase connection works from Vercel serverless environment
Confirm 403 error when accessing another user's interview
resume_bullets: Developed an AI-powered interview simulation platform using Next.js 14 and Gemini 1.5 Flash, enabling real-time multi-turn technical interviews with voice I/O.
Engineered a stateful context engine that reconstructs conversation history per API call using Firebase and Prisma, solving LLM statelessness.
Implemented React Speech Recognition (STT) and Web Speech API (TTS) for seamless hands-free interview experience.
Built a post-interview analytics dashboard with Recharts (RadarChart, RadialBarChart) rendering AI-generated JSON feedback.
Secured user data isolation via Clerk auth and per-request ownership validation across all API routes.

pitfalls.solution: Always send FULL chat history on every API call. Never send just the latest message.
Only start STT in the onEnd callback of SpeechSynthesisUtterance.
Use browserSupportsSpeechRecognition flag — show a fallback text input if false.
Add try/catch around JSON.parse and re-prompt once if it fails. Include 'respond ONLY with valid JSON' in prompt.
Gemini 1.5 Flash: 15 RPM. Add loading state and retry with 2s delay. Show 'AI is thinking...'.
Use a PrismaClient singleton pattern in lib/prisma.ts to avoid exhausting DB connections.
Run npm run build locally first. Fix all TypeScript errors before pushing.
Add Shadcn Skeleton loading states for every async operation.
